issues.step: W1-1 turn 9 (request_0010) report; also no step after turn 6
issues.what: compare_media flagged four sound-difference spans (A 55.5-57.5, 60.0-61.5, 79.5-81.5, 82.0-84.0 s) and its Next line said to 'say what A shows and what B shows there', but the workspace never ran ASR on the source E12 or checked those spans. It then reported COMPLETED with 'The exact speech removed from source 43.6-59.7 s and the semantic content of the four sound differences remain undetermined. A source-audio transcription comparison was not established.'
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches the student to pass on unexplained 'altered' candidates and to file a cheap, decisive check (ASR on the source, or ASR/compare on the flagged ranges) under 'could not be determined'.
issues.ideal: Before reporting, run INSPECT asr on E12 (or on the flagged ranges), then state the source speech in 43.6-59.7 s and whether the speech in each sound span really differs or only the audio signal does.

issues.step: W1-1 turns 6-7 (request_0007, request_0008) and report F3
issues.what: Six boundary frames (E25-E30) were pulled 'to allow visual comparison across the suspected cut', but the report never describes them: F3 says 'they do not establish the depicted content ... No side-by-side visual description is inferred'. It still cites E25-E30 as 'Supporting frame records' for the deletion.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches pulling frames for show and citing them as support without using what they show.
issues.ideal: Describe what the source frames show just before 43.6 s and just after 59.7 s, and what A shows at 44.1/44.5 s, then cite them for that statement; otherwise skip the extraction.

issues.what: The rationale says 'E24 identifies a candidate omission of E22's 43.6-59.7 seconds'. E22 appears nowhere in the workspace's prior observations; turn 6 targeted E12, and E22 shows up only later in the GIA record labels.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: The student learns to cite evidence ids it has never seen.
issues.ideal: Refer to the source as E12 (or R2), the id that is visible in the state.

issues.what: F4 cites E11 only as 'obtained a speech transcription'. The transcript itself shows the join: segment [35.12-45.68 s] ends with a broken sentence ('All of this optimism is allowing people where they were talking a month ago.') right at the A 44.3 s cut. That was never used as corroborating evidence.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches citing a tool result for its existence rather than its content, and so misses easy corroboration of an edit.
issues.ideal: Note that A's speech at about 44 s jumps mid-sentence, consistent with the 16.1 s removal, and cite E11 for it.

issues.what: T1 is the overall task copied verbatim ('The given video circulated online. Find its original source video and determine ...'), with no decomposition into source search, whole-video comparison, dates and audio check.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: The coordinator learns to forward the case text instead of writing a scoped task.
issues.ideal: Keep one workspace, but list concrete steps: find the source, run compare_media, characterize each flagged span (picture and speech), and look up the source's dates.

issues.what: GIA reads E29 ('cited by the report but not attached; view it before answering'), but the FINISH answer uses nothing from E29, and E30 and the other frames are left unread.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches a ritual record read that does not feed the answer.
issues.ideal: Read a record only when the answer depends on its content (e.g. to confirm the cut boundary visually), and then use it in the answer.

issues.what: Frame times are copied as raw floats: 'Material A at 44.110733333333336 and 44.51113333333333 s'.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches dumping unrounded machine numbers into reports.

good_patterns: After the first query hit a provider error (DDGSException), the second query was shortened and rephrased instead of repeated verbatim, and it found the source.

The candidate R2 was checked with a whole-video compare_media before being called the source. The removed interval (B 43.6-59.7 s, 16.1 s, at A 44.3 s) and all four sound-span times were copied exactly from E24, not from the coarser content_match line (44.0/60.2).
Dates are worded correctly: 'These dates establish the history of this copy, not that it was the earliest upload', and the answer says 'earliest publication is not established'.
Sound flags are hedged as algorithmic detections ('do not establish changed words or deliberate audio editing') instead of being presented as proven audio edits.
cannot_judge: Whether 'Bloomberg Technology', 'SPACEX VALUATION JUMPS TO $350B' and 'Katie Roof' (turn 1-3 rationales and query) are actually visible in frames E3/E5: the images are not rendered and OCR failed, so I could not rule out hidden knowledge.
What READ_RECORD E29 returned to GIA: not shown in the rendering.
The end of F4's limitation ('…[+144 chars]') and E24's truncated limitations.
The verifier flagged 'unsupported_assertion/critical', yet the REVISED ANSWER is identical to the original. Which sentence was flagged, and whether that flag was right, cannot be seen here.
summary: This is a clean A-family chain: text search, whole-video compare_media on the matched candidate, a date lookup, and a well-hedged report and answer whose removed-interval and sound-span times match the tool output exactly. The main weakness is that the four flagged sound differences and the 16 s of removed speech were left 'undetermined' without the cheap check that would settle them (ASR on the source), and the six boundary frames were extracted but never described, yet still cited. Smaller issues: a rationale cites an unseen id (E22), the GIA task text is a verbatim copy of the case, and the round-2 record read feeds nothing into the answer. The exported revised answer is identical to the pre-verification answer.
